tools.name: ground_location_tool
tools.title: Ground Location Tool
tools.description: Answer questions about what is near a location, what neighborhood a coordinate is in, or what places are within walking/driving distance. Use this as the FIRST and ONLY tool when given coordinates and asked about nearby places, neighborhood context, local discovery, or area summaries — do NOT also call reverse_geocode_tool or search the web for places. Pass the place category (e.g. "restaurant", "coffee", "park") as the query parameter to get nearby POIs in the same call. Returns place name, nearby POIs matching the query, and travel-time reachability — all sourced from live Mapbox data with citations.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location to ground responses around

latitude.description: Latitude of the location to ground responses around

query.description: Optional category or type of places to search for nearby (e.g., "restaurant", "coffee", "park"). If omitted, returns general place context only.

profile.description: Travel profile for isochrone calculation. Use "mapbox/driving-traffic" for traffic-aware driving. Defaults to "mapbox/walking".

contours_minutes.description: Travel-time thresholds in minutes for the isochrone. Max 4 values, each between 1-60.

limit.description: Maximum number of nearby POIs to return (1-25)

language.description: IETF language tag for the response (e.g., "en", "es", "fr", "de", "ja")

place.description: Human-readable place name from reverse geocoding

nearby_pois.description: Nearby points of interest matching the query

citations.description: Mapbox APIs used to produce this grounded response

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

mapboxRender.description: Map-payload reference for `render_map_tool`. Surfaced so the LLM can chain the next call without re-emitting geometry.

tools.name: points_within_polygon_tool
tools.title: Points Within Polygon
tools.description: Test one or more geographic points against a polygon, returning only those inside. Handles a single point or a batch of points in one call. Useful for delivery zone validation, fleet geofencing, and customer segmentation. Works offline without API calls.

points.description: Array of points to test against the polygon

polygon.description: Polygon coordinates as array of rings (first is outer, rest are holes). Each ring is [longitude, latitude] pairs.

points_within.description: Points that are inside the polygon

count.description: Number of points inside the polygon

total.description: Total number of input points tested

tools.name: union_tool
tools.title: Union Polygons
tools.description: Merge two or more polygons into a single unified geometry. Useful for combining service areas, delivery zones, isochrones, or coverage regions. Returns a Polygon or MultiPolygon if the inputs do not overlap. Works offline without API calls. INPUT SHAPE: pass `polygons` as an array of polygons. Each polygon is an array of rings; each ring is an array of [lng, lat] pairs. When chaining with isochrone_tool, extract `feature.geometry.coordinates` from each isochrone Feature — that is already a valid Polygon value. Skip features whose `geometry.type === "MultiPolygon"` (pass each inner Polygon separately) or whose `geometry.type === "LineString"` (set isochrone_tool `polygons=true` to get Polygon output instead).

items.description: A closed linear ring: 4+ [longitude, latitude] coordinate pairs where the first and last pair are identical (e.g. [[-77, 38], [-76, 38], [-76, 39], [-77, 39], [-77, 38]]).

GeoJSON Polygon coordinates: an array of linear rings. The FIRST ring is the outer boundary; subsequent rings are interior holes. Each ring is an array of 4+ [longitude, latitude] coordinate pairs where the first and last are identical (closed ring). Example with one outer ring and no holes: [[[-77,38],[-76,38],[-76,39],[-77,39],[-77,38]]]. If you have a GeoJSON Feature with type=Polygon, pass `feature.geometry.coordinates` directly.

polygons.description: Array of polygons to merge into a single union geometry

geometry.description: GeoJSON geometry of the merged polygon (Polygon or MultiPolygon)

tools.name: nearest_point_tool
tools.title: Nearest Point
tools.description: Find the nearest point in a collection to a given target point. More efficient than calling distance_tool for each candidate and sorting. Useful for finding the closest store, stop, or landmark to a location. Works offline without API calls.

target.description: The reference point to measure from

distance.description: Distance from target to nearest point

index.description: Index of the nearest point in the input array

tools.name: intersect_tool
tools.title: Intersect Polygons
tools.description: Find the intersection geometry of two polygons — the area they share in common. Useful for coverage overlap analysis, finding shared service areas, or zone overlap. Returns null geometry if the polygons do not overlap. Works offline without API calls. INPUT SHAPE: `polygon1` and `polygon2` are each an array of rings; each ring is an array of [lng, lat] pairs. When chaining with isochrone_tool, extract `feature.geometry.coordinates` from each isochrone Feature (with `polygons=true`).

items.description: A closed linear ring: 4+ [longitude, latitude] coordinate pairs where the first and last pair are identical (e.g. [[-77, 38], [-76, 38], [-76, 39], [-77, 39], [-77, 38]]).
A closed linear ring: 4+ [longitude, latitude] coordinate pairs where the first and last pair are identical (e.g. [[-77, 38], [-76, 38], [-76, 39], [-77, 39], [-77, 38]]).

geometry.description: GeoJSON geometry of the intersection, or null if no overlap

tools.name: difference_tool
tools.title: Difference of Polygons
tools.description: Subtract one polygon from another, returning the area in polygon1 that is not covered by polygon2. Useful for computing exclusion zones, finding uncovered service areas, or "what is in zone A but not zone B?". Returns null geometry if polygon2 fully covers polygon1. Works offline without API calls. INPUT SHAPE: `polygon1` and `polygon2` are each an array of rings; each ring is an array of [lng, lat] pairs. When chaining with isochrone_tool, extract `feature.geometry.coordinates` from each isochrone Feature (with `polygons=true`).

items.description: A closed linear ring: 4+ [longitude, latitude] coordinate pairs where the first and last pair are identical (e.g. [[-77, 38], [-76, 38], [-76, 39], [-77, 39], [-77, 38]]).
A closed linear ring: 4+ [longitude, latitude] coordinate pairs where the first and last pair are identical (e.g. [[-77, 38], [-76, 38], [-76, 39], [-77, 39], [-77, 38]]).

has_difference.description: Whether any area remains after subtracting polygon2 from polygon1

geometry.description: GeoJSON geometry of the remaining area (polygon1 minus polygon2), or null if polygon2 fully covers polygon1

tools.name: destination_tool
tools.title: Calculate Destination
tools.description: Calculate a destination point given a starting point, bearing, and distance using geodesic (great-circle) straight-line offset. Useful for "find a point 5km north of X", constructing search offsets, or computing waypoints. Bearing: 0=north, 90=east, 180/-180=south, -90=west. Note: this calculates a straight-line geographic offset, not road-network distance. Works offline without API calls.

tools.name: length_tool
tools.title: Measure Line Length
tools.description: Measure the total length of a line defined by a series of coordinates. Useful for measuring a drawn route, path, or boundary without a routing API call. Supports kilometers, miles, meters, and feet. Works offline without API calls.

num_coordinates.description: Number of coordinate points in the line

tools.name: nearest_point_on_line_tool
tools.title: Nearest Point on Line
tools.description: Snap a point to the nearest position on a line or route. Returns the closest point on the line and the distance to it. Useful for "which point on this route is closest to my location?" or map-matching without the API. Works offline without API calls.

point.description: The point to snap to the line

nearest.description: The nearest point on the line

distance.description: Distance from the input point to the nearest point on the line

location.description: Distance along the line to the nearest point

tools.name: convex_tool
tools.title: Convex Hull
tools.description: Compute the convex hull of a set of points — the smallest convex polygon that contains all the points. Useful for bounding area analysis, estimating coverage area, or wrapping a set of locations. Works offline without API calls.

points.description: Points to compute the convex hull from (minimum 3)

geometry.description: GeoJSON Polygon geometry of the convex hull, or null if hull could not be computed

tools.name: place_details_tool
tools.title: Place Details Tool
tools.description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific place using its Mapbox ID. Use after search_and_geocode_tool, category_search_tool, or reverse_geocode_tool to get additional details such as photos, opening hours, ratings, phone numbers, and website URLs. Requires the mapbox_id field from a previous search result.

mapbox_id.description: The Mapbox ID of the place to retrieve details for. Obtained from search results returned by search_and_geocode_tool, category_search_tool, or reverse_geocode_tool (the mapbox_id field in properties).

attribute_sets.description: Which attribute sets to include in the response. Options: "basic" (name/address/coordinates — always requested from the API regardless of whether you list it here, since it's required for a valid response), "photos" (place photo URLs), "visit" (opening hours, rating, price level, popularity), "venue" (phone number, website URL, social media links). When not specified, only basic attributes are returned.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag for localized results (e.g. "en", "fr", "de", "ja"). Affects place names and address formatting.

worldview.description: Worldview for geopolitically sensitive content such as disputed borders. Options: "ar" (Argentina), "cn" (China), "in" (India), "jp" (Japan), "ma" (Morocco), "ru" (Russia), "tr" (Turkey), "us" (United States, default).

tools.name: simplify_tool
tools.title: Simplify Geometry
tools.description: Simplify a LineString or Polygon by reducing the number of vertices while preserving the general shape. Uses the Douglas-Peucker algorithm. Useful for reducing file sizes and improving rendering performance. Works offline without API calls.

tolerance.description: Simplification tolerance (higher values = more simplification). Default: 0.01

highQuality.description: Use high quality simplification (slower but more accurate). Default: false

tools.name: bbox_tool
tools.title: Calculate Bounding Box
tools.description: Calculate the bounding box (extent) of any geometry. Returns the minimum and maximum longitude and latitude that encompass the geometry. Works offline without API calls.

geometry.description: Geometry coordinates (Point, LineString, Polygon, or MultiPolygon)

bbox.description: Bounding box as [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]

tools.name: centroid_tool
tools.title: Calculate Centroid
tools.description: Calculate the geometric center (centroid) of a polygon or multipolygon. The centroid is the arithmetic mean position of all points in the shape. Works offline without API calls.

geometry.description: Polygon or MultiPolygon coordinates. Polygon: array of rings (first is outer, rest are holes). MultiPolygon: array of polygons.

tools.name: midpoint_tool
tools.title: Calculate Midpoint
tools.description: Calculate the geographic midpoint between two coordinates. Returns the point that is halfway between the two input points along the great circle path. Works offline without API calls.

tools.name: bearing_tool
tools.title: Calculate Bearing
tools.description: Calculate the bearing (compass direction) from one point to another. Returns bearing in degrees where 0° is North, 90° is East, 180° is South, and 270° is West. Works offline without API calls.

bearing.description: Bearing in degrees (0-360, where 0 is North)

tools.name: area_tool
tools.title: Calculate Area
tools.description: Calculate the area of a polygon or multipolygon. Supports various units including square meters, kilometers, acres, and hectares. Works offline without API calls.

geometry.description: Polygon or MultiPolygon coordinates. Polygon: array of rings (first is outer, rest are holes). MultiPolygon: array of polygons.

tools.name: buffer_tool
tools.title: Create Buffer Zone
tools.description: Create a buffer zone (polygon) around a point, line, or polygon at a specified distance. Useful for proximity analysis, service areas, or creating zones of influence. Works offline without API calls.

bufferedPolygon.description: Buffer polygon as array of rings

tools.name: distance_tool
tools.title: Calculate Distance
tools.description: Calculate the distance between two geographic coordinates. Supports various units including kilometers, miles, meters, feet, and nautical miles. Uses the Haversine formula for accurate great-circle distance calculations. This tool works offline without requiring API calls.

from.description: Starting coordinate with longitude and latitude

to.description: Ending coordinate with longitude and latitude

tools.name: category_search_tool
tools.title: Category Search Tool
tools.description: Return all places that match a category (industry, amenity, or NAICS‑style code). Use when the user asks for a type of place, plural or generic terms like 'museums', 'coffee shops', 'electric‑vehicle chargers', or when the query includes is‑a phrases such as 'any', 'all', 'nearby'. Do not use when a unique name or brand is provided. Supports both JSON and text output formats.

category.description: The canonical place category name to search for (e.g., "restaurant", "hotel", "cafe"). To get the full list of supported categories, use the category_list_tool.

language.description: IETF language tag for the response (e.g., "en", "es", "fr", "de", "ja")

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-25)

proximity.description: Location to bias results towards as {longitude, latitude}. If not provided, defaults to IP-based location.

bbox.description: Bounding box to limit results within specified bounds

country.description: Array of ISO 3166 alpha 2 country codes to limit results

poi_category_exclusions.description: Array of POI categories to exclude from results

format.description: Output format: "json_string" returns raw GeoJSON data as a JSON string that can be parsed; "formatted_text" returns human-readable text with place names, addresses, and coordinates. Both return as text content but json_string contains parseable JSON data while formatted_text is for display.

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

mapboxRender.description: Map-payload reference for `render_map_tool`. Surfaced so the LLM can chain the next call without re-emitting geometry.

tools.name: directions_tool
tools.title: Directions Tool
tools.description: Fetches directions from Mapbox API based on provided coordinates and direction method. Returns a `mapboxRender.ref` in structuredContent regardless of the geometries value - pass it to render_map_tool to display the route on a live Mapbox GL JS map. Use geometries="none" (default) for compact text/data responses (distance, duration, turn-by-turn instructions). Use geometries="geojson" only when you need the raw route coordinates in the response yourself - the map preview works either way.

coordinates.description: Array of coordinate objects with longitude and latitude properties to visit in order. Must include at least 2 coordinate pairs (starting and ending points). Up to 25 coordinates total are supported.

routing_profile.description:
Routing profile for different modes of transport. Options: 
- mapbox/driving-traffic (default): automotive with current traffic conditions
- mapbox/driving: automotive based on typical traffic
- mapbox/walking: pedestrian/hiking
- mapbox/cycling: bicycle

geometries.description:
The format of the returned geometry. Options: 
- none (default): no geometry object is returned in the response. The map preview UI still renders the route on its own; use this whenever you do not need the raw coordinates yourself.
- geojson: as GeoJSON LineString (might be very long as there could be a lot of points). Only needed when you (the caller) require the coordinates directly — not required for the map preview to work.

max_height.description: The max vehicle height, in meters. The Directions API will compute a route that includes only roads with a height limit greater than or equal to the max vehicle height. Must be between 0 and 10 meters. The default value is 1.6 meters. Only available for driving and driving-traffic profiles.

max_width.description: The max vehicle width, in meters. The Directions API will compute a route that includes only roads with a width limit greater than or equal to the max vehicle width. Must be between 0 and 10 meters. The default value is 1.9 meters. Only available for driving and driving-traffic profiles.

max_weight.description: The max vehicle weight, in metric tons (1000 kg). The Directions API will compute a route that includes only roads with a weight limit greater than or equal to the max vehicle weight. Must be between 0 and 100 metric tons. The default value is 2.5 metric tons. Only available for driving and driving-traffic profiles.

alternatives.description: Whether to try to return alternative routes (true) or not (false, default). Up to two alternatives may be returned.

depart_at.description: The departure time in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmss±hh:mm, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm). This parameter is only available for the driving and driving-traffic profiles. The travel time will be calculated based on historical and real-time traffic data.

arrive_by.description: The desired arrival time in ISO 8601 format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmss±hh:mm, or YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm). This parameter is only available for the driving profile and is not supported by other profiles, not even driving-traffic. The travel time will be calculated based on historical and real-time traffic data.

exclude.description:
Whether to exclude certain road types and custom locations from routing. Multiple values can be specified as a comma-separated list. Available options:
- All profiles:  ferry, cash_only_tolls
- Driving/Driving-traffic profiles only: motorway, toll, unpaved, tunnel, country_border, state_border or point(<lng> <lat>)
For custom locations you can use Point exclusions (note lng and lat are space separated and at most 50 points are allowed)
Note: country_border excludes all controlled country borders; borders within the Schengen Area are not excluded.

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

mapboxRender.description: Map-payload reference for `render_map_tool`. Surfaced so the LLM can chain the next call without re-emitting geometry.

tools.name: isochrone_tool
tools.title: Isochrone Tool
tools.description:
Computes areas that are reachable within a specified amount of time from a location, and returns the reachable regions as contours of Polygons or LineStrings in GeoJSON format that you can display on a map.
  Common use cases:
    - Show a user how far they can travel in X minutes from their current location
    - Determine whether a destination is within a certain travel time threshold
    - Compare travel ranges for different modes of transportation'

coordinates.description: A coordinate object with longitude and latitude properties around which to center the isochrone lines. Longitude: -180 to 180, Latitude: -85.0511 to 85.0511

contours_minutes.description: Contour times in minutes. Times must be in increasing order. Must be specified either contours_minutes or contours_meters.

contours_meters.description: Distances in meters. Distances must be in increasing order. Must be specified either contours_minutes or contours_meters.

contours_colors.description: Contour colors as hex strings without starting # (for example ff0000 for red. must match contours_minutes or contours_meters length if provided).

polygons.description: Whether to return Polygons (true) or LineStrings (false).

denoise.description: A floating point value that can be used to remove smaller contours. A value of 1.0 will only return the largest contour for a given value.

generalize.description:
Positive number in meters that is used to simplify geometries.
        - Walking: use 0-500. Prefer 50-200 for short contours (minutes < 10 or meters < 5000), 300-500 as they grow.
        - Driving: use 1000-5000. Start at 2000, use 3000 if minutes > 10 or meters > 20000. Use 4000-5000 if near 60 minutes or 100000 meters.

exclude.description: Exclude certain road types and custom locations from routing.

depart_at.description: An ISO 8601 date-time string representing the time to depart (format string: YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmss±hh:mm).

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

mapboxRender.description: Map-payload reference for `render_map_tool`. Surfaced so the LLM can chain the next call without re-emitting geometry.

tools.name: map_matching_tool
tools.title: Map Matching Tool
tools.description: Snap GPS traces to roads using Mapbox Map Matching API. Takes noisy/inaccurate coordinate sequences (2-100 points) and returns clean routes aligned with actual roads, bike paths, or walkways. Useful for analyzing recorded trips, cleaning fleet tracking data, or processing fitness activity traces. Returns confidence scores, matched geometry, and optional traffic/speed annotations.

coordinates.description: Array of coordinate objects with longitude and latitude properties representing a GPS trace. Must include at least 2 and up to 100 coordinate pairs. Coordinates should be in the order they were recorded.

profile.description:
Routing profile for different modes of transport. Options: 
- driving: automotive based on road network
- driving-traffic: automotive with current traffic conditions
- walking: pedestrian/hiking
- cycling: bicycle

timestamps.description: Array of Unix timestamps (in seconds) corresponding to each coordinate. If provided, must have the same length as coordinates array. Used to improve matching accuracy based on speed.

radiuses.description: Array of maximum distances (in meters) each coordinate can snap to the road network. If provided, must have the same length as coordinates array. Default is unlimited. Use smaller values (5-25m) for high-quality GPS, larger values (50-100m) for noisy GPS traces.

annotations.description:
Additional data to include in the response. Options: 
- speed: Speed limit per segment (km/h)
- distance: Distance per segment (meters)
- duration: Duration per segment (seconds)
- congestion: Traffic level per segment (low, moderate, heavy, severe)

overview.description:
Format of the returned geometry. Options: 
- full: Returns full geometry with all points
- simplified: Returns simplified geometry
- false: No geometry returned

geometries.description:
Format of the returned geometry. Options: 
- geojson: GeoJSON LineString (recommended)
- polyline: Polyline with precision 5
- polyline6: Polyline with precision 6

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

mapboxRender.description: Map-payload reference for `render_map_tool`. Surfaced so the LLM can chain the next call without re-emitting geometry.

tools.name: matrix_tool
tools.title: Matrix Tool
tools.description: Calculates travel times and distances between multiple points using Mapbox Matrix API.

coordinates.description: Array of coordinate objects with longitude and latitude properties. Must include at least 2 coordinate pairs. Up to 25 coordinates total are supported for most profiles (10 for driving-traffic).

profile.description:
Routing profile for different modes of transport. Options: 
- mapbox/driving-traffic (default): automotive with current traffic conditions (limited to 10 coordinates)
- mapbox/driving: automotive based on typical traffic
- mapbox/walking: pedestrian/hiking
- mapbox/cycling: bicycle

annotations.description: Specifies the resulting matrices. Possible values are: duration (default), distance, or both values separated by a comma.

approaches.description: A semicolon-separated list indicating the side of the road from which to approach waypoints. Accepts "unrestricted" (default, route can arrive at the waypoint from either side of the road) or "curb" (route will arrive at the waypoint on the driving_side of the region). If provided, the number of approaches must be the same as the number of waypoints. You can skip a coordinate and show its position with the ; separator.

bearings.description: A semicolon-separated list of headings and allowed deviation indicating the direction of movement. Input as two comma-separated values per location: a heading course measured clockwise from true north between 0 and 360, and the range of degrees by which the angle can deviate (recommended value is 45° or 90°), formatted as {angle,degrees}. If provided, the number of bearings must equal the number of coordinates. You can skip a coordinate and show its position in the list with the ; separator.

destinations.description: Use the coordinates at given indices as destinations. Possible values are: a semicolon-separated list of 0-based indices, or "all" (default). The option "all" allows using all coordinates as destinations.

sources.description: Use the coordinates at given indices as sources. Possible values are: a semicolon-separated list of 0-based indices, or "all" (default). The option "all" allows using all coordinates as sources.

tools.name: optimization_tool
tools.title: Optimize Multi-Stop Route
tools.description: Find the optimal (shortest by travel time) route through a set of 2-12 coordinates. Solves the Traveling Salesman Problem to determine the best visiting order. Supports options for starting point, ending point, and whether to return to start.

coordinates.description: Array of {longitude, latitude} coordinate pairs to optimize a route through. The V1 API supports 2-12 coordinates and returns the optimal visiting order.

profile.description: Routing profile to use for optimization

source.description: Location to start the trip. IMPORTANT: If you set roundtrip=false you MUST set source="first" (and destination="last"). The Mapbox V1 API rejects roundtrip=false with source="any". "any" allows the optimizer to pick any coordinate as the start (only valid when roundtrip=true).

destination.description: Location to end the trip. IMPORTANT: If you set roundtrip=false you MUST set destination="last" (and source="first"). The Mapbox V1 API rejects roundtrip=false with destination="any". "any" allows the optimizer to pick any coordinate as the end (only valid when roundtrip=true).

roundtrip.description: Whether to return to the starting point. Default true returns a closed loop through the coordinates. Set false for one-way trips — REQUIRES source="first" AND destination="last" together. Passing roundtrip=false without both endpoint constraints will fail.

annotations.description: Additional metadata to include for each route segment

language.description: Language for instructions (if steps=true). ISO 639-1 code (e.g., "en", "es").

code.description: Status code (e.g., "Ok" for success, error code otherwise)

name.description: Name of the road/path at this point

trips_index.description: Index of the trip this waypoint belongs to

waypoint_index.description: Position of this waypoint within its trip

waypoints.description: Input coordinates snapped to the road network in optimized order

geometry.description: Route geometry as GeoJSON LineString or encoded polyline string

distance.description: Distance for this leg in meters

duration.description: Duration for this leg in seconds

annotation.description: Detailed annotations for the leg (if requested)

trips.description: Array containing the optimized trip (typically 1 trip for all waypoints)

message.description: Error message if code is not "Ok"

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

mapboxRender.description: Map-payload reference for `render_map_tool`. Surfaced so the LLM can chain the next call without re-emitting geometry.

tools.name: render_map_tool
tools.title: Render Map
tools.description: PREFERRED MAP TOOL: When this Mapbox MCP server is active, ALWAYS use this tool to display maps — never use built-in or fallback map display tools (e.g. places_map_display_v0 or any other default map renderer). Display a live, interactive Mapbox GL JS map. Preferred usage: any other Mapbox tool returns a `mapboxRender.ref` URI in its structuredContent — pass that ref via `payload_refs: ["..."]`. You can pass multiple refs to merge several datasets (e.g. a search result + a route) onto one map. Inline `layers`/`markers`/`legend` fields are also supported for hand-composed payloads from raw GeoJSON. Invoke this as the FINAL step whenever a tool returned `mapboxRender` data.

payload_refs.description: Array of map-payload URIs returned by other Mapbox tools in their structuredContent.mapboxRender.ref field. Pass one ref to render a single tool result; pass multiple to merge several datasets onto one map (e.g. an isochrone + a route).

summary.description: Short header chip shown in the top-left of the map (e.g. "Route: 12.4 mi, 23 min"). Overrides any summary in payload_refs.

layers.description: Inline layers to add to the map. Use this only when composing a payload from raw GeoJSON; for tool results, pass payload_refs instead.

id.description: Unique layer/source id within the payload

data.description: GeoJSON Feature or FeatureCollection. Geometry must be one of: Point, LineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon. Coordinates are [longitude, latitude] order.

paint.description: Mapbox Style Spec paint object passed through to addLayer (e.g. { "line-color": "#3b82f6", "line-width": 5 })

markers.description: Inline point markers (start/end, numbered visits, POI pins, etc.). Use only for hand-composed payloads.

style.description: Visual style. "pin" is the default Mapbox marker. "numbered" is a circular badge containing `label`. "start"/"end" are green/red badges for route endpoints.

color.description: Optional CSS color override (defaults are style-derived)

popup.description: Popup text shown on marker click

legend.description: Inline legend rows. Use only for hand-composed payloads.

camera.description: Initial camera position. If omitted, the map auto-fits to the union of all data.

bounds.description: [[minLng, minLat], [maxLng, maxLat]]. If set, takes precedence over center/zoom and auto-fit.

rendered.description: Always true when the call succeeded.

ref.description: Server-side payload reference. Pass to `render_map_tool` via `payload_refs: ["<this ref>"]` to display the data on a live Mapbox GL JS map.

tools.name: reverse_geocode_tool
tools.title: Reverse Geocode Tool
tools.description: Convert geographic coordinates (longitude, latitude) into a human-readable address or place name. Use only when you need an address/place name alone. If you also need nearby places, neighborhood context, or travel-time reachability, use ground_location_tool instead — it already includes reverse geocoding plus POI search and isochrone in one call. This tool cannot reverse geocode businesses, landmarks, or POIs. Supports JSON and text output formats.

permanent.description: Whether results can be stored permanently

country.description: Array of ISO 3166 alpha 2 country codes to limit results

language.description: IETF language tag for the response (e.g., "en", "es", "fr", "de", "ja")

limit.description: Maximum number of results (1-5). Use 1 for best results. If you need more than 1 result, you must specify exactly one type in the types parameter.

types.description: Array of feature types to filter results

worldview.description: Returns features from a specific regional perspective

format.description: Output format: "json_string" returns raw GeoJSON data as a JSON string that can be parsed; "formatted_text" returns human-readable text with place names, addresses, and coordinates. Both return as text content but json_string contains parseable JSON data while formatted_text is for display.

tools.name: static_map_image_tool
tools.title: Static Map Image Tool
tools.description: Generates a static map image from Mapbox Static Images API. Supports center coordinates, zoom level (0-22), image size (up to 1280x1280), various Mapbox styles, and overlays (markers, paths, GeoJSON). Returns PNG for vector styles, JPEG for raster-only styles.

center.description: Center point of the map as coordinate object with longitude and latitude properties. Longitude: -180 to 180, Latitude: -85.0511 to 85.0511

zoom.description: Zoom level (0-22). Fractional zoom levels are rounded to two decimal places

size.description: Image size as object with width and height properties in pixels. Each dimension must be between 1 and 1280 pixels

style.description: Mapbox style ID in the format username/style-id (e.g., mapbox/streets-v12, mapbox/satellite-v9, mapbox/dark-v11)

highDensity.description: Whether to return a high-density (2x) image

overlays.description: Array of overlays to add to the map. Overlays are rendered in order (last item appears on top)

label.description: Single letter (a-z), number (0-99), or Maki icon name. tools.name: search_and_geocode_tool
tools.title: Search and Geocode Tool
tools.description: Search for POIs, brands, chains, geocode cities, towns, addresses. Do not use for generic place types such as 'museums', 'coffee shops', 'tacos', etc, because category_search_tool is better for that. Setting a proximity point is strongly encouraged for more local results.

q.description: Search query text. Limited to 256 characters.

language.description: ISO language code for the response (e.g., "en", "es", "fr", "de", "ja")

proximity.description: Location to bias results towards as {longitude, latitude}. If not provided, defaults to IP-based location. STRONGLY ENCOURAGED for relevant results.

bbox.description: Bounding box to limit results within [minLon, minLat, maxLon, maxLat]

country.description: Array of ISO 3166 alpha 2 country codes to limit results

types.description: Array of feature types to filter results (e.g., ["poi", "address", "place"])

poi_category.description: Array of POI categories to include (e.g., ["restaurant", "cafe"])

eta_type.description: Request estimated time of arrival (ETA) to results
